claims.statement: claims-mcp is a stdio MCP server that maintains a catalog of claims stored as a JSON file in the repo, and the repo contains a skill tailored to using it for claims auditing

evidence.summary: All 11 children supported. Concept coverage: stdio MCP server (0002, 0004) on rmcp (0003); JSON catalog in the repo (0005 + durability 0006-0009, 0018); traceability (0010/0011); FEVER (0012/0013); IEEE 1012 levels/methods (0014); V&V gap reporting (0015); tailored skill (0016) wired via .mcp.json (0017); spec conformance (0019).

verdicts.rationale: Every element of concept.md maps to a supported child claim (EVD-0039).

claims.statement: The server speaks MCP over stdio, and stdout carries only JSON-RPC protocol messages (logs go to stderr)

evidence.locator: target/release/claims-mcp driven over stdio (initialize, tools/list, 8 tools/call) in a temp dir
evidence.summary: 10 stdout lines, all JSON-RPC 2.0 messages (0 non-JSON-RPC lines); 0 bytes on stderr; process exited 0 when stdin closed.
tracing_subscriber fmt is configured with .with_writer(std::io::stderr) and ANSI disabled; the server is served via rmcp::transport::stdio_pipes().

verdicts.rationale: Live stdio run produced only JSON-RPC lines on stdout and nothing on stderr; code routes tracing to stderr.

claims.statement: The server is built on the rmcp crate: Cargo.toml depends on rmcp and the tools are registered with rmcp's #[tool_router]/#[tool_handler] macros
claims.source: user prompt: 'Please make sure to use the rmcp crate'

evidence.summary: Cargo.toml declares rmcp 3.7.0 with features server, macros, transport-io; cargo tree resolves rmcp v3.7.0 as a direct dependency.
The ClaimsServer impl is annotated #[tool_router] with 10 #[tool] methods, and ServerHandler is implemented via rmcp's #[tool_handler] macro.

verdicts.rationale: rmcp 3.7.0 is a resolved direct dependency and the tool surface is built with its tool_router/tool_handler macros.

claims.statement: tools/list returns exactly the 10 tools of spec section 4: add_claim, add_claims, get_claim, list_claims, update_claim, retire_claim, add_evidence, record_verdict, trace, audit_report

evidence.summary: Returned exactly: add_claim, add_claims, add_evidence, audit_report, get_claim, list_claims, record_verdict, retire_claim, trace, update_claim (10 tools); read-only hints on audit_report, get_claim, list_claims, trace.

verdicts.rationale: tools/list on the release binary returned exactly the 10 spec tools, no more, no fewer.

claims.statement: The catalog is persisted as a JSON document with schema_version 1 at the --catalog path (default claims.json, env CLAIMS_CATALOG)
claims.source: concept.md: 'stored as a json file in the repo'; spec 3.1, 5

evidence.locator: release binary run with no --catalog in a temp dir; then with CLAIMS_CATALOG=<tmp>/env.json
evidence.summary: Without --catalog, add_claim created ./claims.json starting with "schema_version": 1; with CLAIMS_CATALOG set, env.json was created containing CLM-0001.

verdicts.rationale: Default path and env override both observed creating a schema_version 1 JSON catalog.

claims.statement: A catalog mutation whose operation fails leaves the catalog file byte-identical

evidence.summary: Passes: a mutate whose closure adds a claim and then returns Err leaves the catalog file bytes equal to the pre-call bytes.

verdicts.rationale: Test directly compares file bytes before and after a failing mutation; passes.

claims.statement: Concurrent writers sharing one catalog file never lose updates

evidence.summary: Passes (and passed 3/3 runs earlier): 4 threads, each with its own CatalogStore on the same file, 10 add_claim mutations each; final read sees 40 claims and load-time validation found no duplicate ids.

verdicts.rationale: Contention test with 4 independent store handles x 10 writes ends with all 40 claims and valid ids, across repeated runs.

claims.statement: A catalog file whose next_claim_seq is not above its highest claim id is rejected on load instead of being used

evidence.summary: Passes: a file with next_claim_seq 1 and claim CLM-0001 makes read return ClaimsError::Validation instead of the catalog.

verdicts.rationale: Test loads exactly the stale-counter case and gets a Validation error rather than a catalog.

claims.statement: Saving an unchanged catalog produces a byte-identical file ending in a newline

evidence.summary: Passes: two saves of the same catalog produce identical bytes and the last byte is a newline.

verdicts.rationale: Test asserts byte equality across two saves and a trailing newline; passes.

claims.statement: trace returns a claim's ancestors via derived_from and its active descendants, each with its shortest depth

evidence.summary: Passes: on root<-mid<-leaf, trace(mid, both) returns ancestor root and descendant leaf; trace(root, down, None) returns depths [1, 2]; max_depth 1 returns one descendant.

verdicts.rationale: trace test shows both directions with shortest depths and depth limiting; its child CLM-0011 (cycle prevention) is supported.

claims.statement: update_claim rejects a derived_from change that would create a cycle or a self-link

evidence.summary: Passes: linking root to its own descendant and linking root to itself both return ClaimsError::Cycle.

verdicts.rationale: Both cycle and self-link updates are asserted to fail with Cycle; passes.

claims.statement: Verdicts use the FEVER labels supported, refuted, not_enough_info and are kept as append-only history per claim

evidence.summary: Both pass: after refuted then not_enough_info, the claim holds 2 verdict records with the first still refuted; verdict labels serialize as snake_case (e.g. not_enough_info).

verdicts.rationale: Labels serialize as the FEVER names and earlier verdicts survive later ones; child CLM-0013 (evidence-backed verdicts) is supported.

claims.statement: record_verdict rejects 'supported' unless it cites evidence on the same claim with stance 'supports'

evidence.summary: Both pass: 'supported' citing only neutral evidence returns Validation; citing evidence attached to a different claim returns ForeignEvidence; citing own supports evidence succeeds.

verdicts.rationale: Tests cover both halves: neutral-only evidence is rejected and evidence from another claim is rejected.

claims.statement: Claims carry an IEEE 1012 integrity level restricted to 1-4 and a verification method (inspection, analysis, demonstration, test, formal_proof)

evidence.summary: Passes: integrity levels 0 and 5 fail to deserialize, 4 succeeds. The tool schema (seen in this session) also lists verification_method values inspection, analysis, demonstration, test, formal_proof.

verdicts.rationale: Range 1-4 enforced at deserialization (0 and 5 rejected); the five verification methods are the enum values exposed in the tool schema.

claims.statement: audit_report returns all eight gap categories (no_evidence, unverified, refuted, not_enough_info, stale, rigor, decomposition, dangling_links) and a traceability matrix

evidence.locator: audit_report tool call (id 10) on release binary
evidence.summary: Response top-level keys: gaps, matrix, totals; gaps keys exactly: dangling_links, decomposition, no_evidence, not_enough_info, refuted, rigor, stale, unverified.

verdicts.rationale: Live report contained exactly the eight gap keys plus totals and matrix.

claims.statement: skills/claims-audit/SKILL.md has valid skill frontmatter and references every one of the server's 10 tools by name
claims.source: concept.md: 'a skill that is tailor-made to use this mcp'

evidence.locator: python frontmatter parse + backticked tool-name scan of skills/claims-audit/SKILL.md
evidence.summary: Frontmatter parses with keys name (claims-audit) and description (551 chars); all 10 tool names appear in backticks; missing list is empty.

verdicts.rationale: Frontmatter parses with name and description, and every server tool is referenced by name.

claims.statement: .mcp.json registers the claims server for this repo with the catalog at claims.json

evidence.summary: .mcp.json defines server 'claims' running cargo run --release --quiet -- --catalog claims.json; this session loaded the mcp__claims__* tools from it and the claims registered here were written to ./claims.json in the repo root.

verdicts.rationale: This very audit runs through the server registered by .mcp.json and writes to ./claims.json.

claims.statement: The store's lock and temp sidecar files are ignored by git

evidence.summary: Both paths are matched by .gitignore lines 2 and 3; git status lists claims.json as untracked but not .claims.json.lock, which exists on disk.

verdicts.rationale: git check-ignore matches both sidecar names and the existing lock file does not appear in git status.

claims.statement: The implementation conforms to the design spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-claims-mcp-design.md

evidence.summary: All 14 children are supported. Together they cover spec section 2 (no command execution), 3.4 rules 3/5/6, section 5 module boundaries, 5.1/6 schema and parse error handling, 5.2 template changes, 6 error mapping and no-unwrap, 9 deliverables and quality gates. Rules 1, 2, 4 and section 4/4.1 are covered under CLM-0001's children (CLM-0004, -0010/-0011, -0012/-0013, -0015).

verdicts.rationale: Every decomposed spec requirement is independently supported; see EVD-0038 for the coverage mapping.

claims.statement: The server never executes commands or spawns processes (no std::process::Command or tokio::process use in src/)

evidence.summary: Only 2 matches: src/main.rs:42 std::process::exit(1) on startup failure, and src/store.rs:328 std::thread::spawn inside the #[cfg(test)] contention test. No Command, tokio::process, or process spawning anywhere in src/.

verdicts.rationale: Exhaustive grep finds no command execution or process spawning; the only hits are process::exit and a test-only thread.

claims.statement: Retired claims reject update_claim, add_evidence, and record_verdict

evidence.summary: Passes, but only asserts add_evidence and update_claim return Retired on a retired claim; record_verdict on a retired claim is not exercised by this test.

evidence.locator: release binary: retire_claim CLM-0001 then record_verdict (id 6), add_evidence (id 7), update_claim (id 8)
evidence.summary: All three calls on the retired claim returned isError=true with text 'claim CLM-0001 is retired'.

verdicts.rationale: The unit test leaves record_verdict uncovered (EVD-0021, neutral), but the live demonstration shows all three operations rejected on a retired claim.

claims.statement: A claim with a blank statement is rejected, and duplicate tags or artifacts are removed keeping the first occurrence

evidence.summary: Both pass: a whitespace-only statement returns Validation; tags ["a"," a ","","b"] are stored as ["a","b"]. Artifacts go through the same clean_list helper (src/catalog.rs:405-406), though only tags are asserted.

verdicts.rationale: Blank statements rejected and duplicate removal shown for tags; artifacts share the same helper.

claims.statement: add_claims is all-or-nothing, and an @N reference must point at an earlier entry of the same batch

evidence.summary: Both pass: a batch whose entry 1 references @1 (not earlier) fails with Validation and the catalog equals its prior state; @0 from entry 1 resolves to the batch's first new id.

verdicts.rationale: Failed batch leaves the catalog equal to its prior state, and a non-earlier @N is rejected.

claims.statement: Only store.rs touches the filesystem and only server.rs (plus main.rs startup) uses rmcp

evidence.locator: per-file grep counts of std::fs|fs::|File:: and rmcp in src/*.rs
evidence.summary: Filesystem references: store.rs 14, every other file 0. rmcp references: server.rs 5, main.rs 2 (ServiceExt and stdio_pipes), every other file 0.

verdicts.rationale: Per-file counts show filesystem access only in store.rs and rmcp only in server.rs and main.rs.

claims.statement: A catalog file with an unsupported schema_version is rejected and left unmodified

evidence.locator: release binary --catalog v2.json (schema_version 2) + add_claim; sha256sum before/after
evidence.summary: add_claim returned isError=true 'catalog v2.json has schema_version 2; this server supports 1'; the file's sha256 was unchanged afterwards.
Passes: reading a schema_version 2 file returns UnsupportedSchema{found: 2}. The test exercises read only, not mutate.

verdicts.rationale: A mutation against a schema_version 2 file errored and the file hash was unchanged; the unit test covers the read path.

claims.statement: Domain errors are returned as tool results with isError true and the error's Display text, not as JSON-RPC protocol errors

evidence.summary: Each domain failure (retired claim x3, 'claim CLM-0099 not found') came back as a normal result with isError=true and the Display text; no JSON-RPC error objects were returned.

verdicts.rationale: Four distinct domain failures all came back as isError results with Display text and no protocol errors.

claims.statement: When the catalog file is not valid JSON, the tool error names the file path and the serde line/column

evidence.summary: Returned isError=true: 'catalog bad.json is not a valid claims catalog: key must be a string at line 2 column 3' (path plus line/column).

verdicts.rationale: Error text includes the catalog path and 'line 2 column 3'.

claims.statement: There is no .unwrap() call in src/ outside #[cfg(test)] code

evidence.summary: No matches anywhere in src/, test code included.

verdicts.rationale: No .unwrap() exists anywhere in src/.

claims.statement: The template's console-subscriber, ctrlc, lazy_static, dotenv dependencies and tokio_unstable rustflag are removed, and dotenvy is used instead of dotenv

evidence.summary: Cargo.toml has no console-subscriber, ctrlc, lazy_static, dotenv, or tracing-log entries; .cargo/ (which held the tokio_unstable rustflag) no longer exists; dotenvy 0.15.7 is declared and main.rs calls dotenvy::dotenv().

verdicts.rationale: All listed template crates and the rustflag config are gone; dotenvy is declared and used.

claims.statement: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --check all pass

evidence.locator: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test
evidence.summary: fmt exited 0 with no diff; clippy finished with no warnings or errors; cargo test: 56 passed, 0 failed.

verdicts.rationale: All three gates were run in this audit and passed.

claims.statement: Every pub item in src/ has a doc comment

evidence.locator: python scan of src/*.rs non-test pub items for a preceding /// line
evidence.summary: Flagged 5 items (model.rs:44 macro pub struct $name, ClaimKind, ClaimLevel, VerificationMethod, CurrentVerdict); manual reading shows all 5 have doc comments separated by multi-line #[derive(...)] attributes, and $name receives its docs via $(#[$meta])* from documented invocations. The scan's flags are false positives.
0 'missing documentation' warnings.

verdicts.rationale: rustdoc missing_docs reports nothing, and the 5 heuristic flags were checked by hand and are documented.

claims.statement: README.md documents build, configuration, the tool reference, and skill installation via cp -r skills/claims-audit ~/.claude/skills/

evidence.locator: README.md sections Build (l.21), Run (l.27, CLAIMS_CATALOG table l.35), Tools (l.68), Install the skill (l.59-63)
evidence.summary: README has Build with cargo build --release, a configuration table (--catalog, CLAIMS_CATALOG, RUST_LOG), a 10-row tool table, and 'cp -r skills/claims-audit ~/.claude/skills/'.

verdicts.rationale: All four required README topics are present, including the exact install command.

claims.statement: A timestamped changelog entry exists under changelog/

verdicts.rationale: Two UTC-timestamped changelog files exist.

claims.statement: The implementation plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-claims-mcp.md reproduces the committed source: its code blocks and expected test counts match the repo

evidence.locator: python: plan rust code blocks reassembled per module vs src/*.rs; plan 'N passed' strings vs cargo test
evidence.summary: Only main.rs matches the plan; error.rs, model.rs, catalog.rs, report.rs, store.rs, server.rs all differ (post-review fixes were never back-ported). The plan's only expected test count is 46; cargo test reports 56.

verdicts.rationale: Six of seven modules differ from the plan's code blocks and the plan's expected test count (46) does not match the actual 56; following the plan today would reproduce pre-review code.
